programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.about: Computing within a liberal arts degree, connecting mathematical and software methods with another discipline.
programmes.overview: You study computing in a broad liberal arts setting and combine the major with a minor or second major in a related area, such as applied mathematics, engineering, economics or interactive media. Advanced students can join faculty research. The published study plan places study away in the autumn of the third year, with a second semester requiring permission. The degree develops mathematical problem solving, programming, communication and teamwork.
programmes.ib: No programme-specific IB grade threshold is published on the reviewed page; strong algebra, pre-calculus or calculus preparation is encouraged.

programmes.name: Mechanical Engineering
programmes.about: Mechanical and thermal systems studied through an integrated science, engineering and design curriculum.
programmes.overview: The programme connects mechanics, materials, thermal systems and design with the wider liberal arts curriculum. A shared science and engineering foundation precedes the specialism. In the final-year design project, teams define a practical problem, work within realistic constraints, build or simulate a solution and test it. The programme describes internships as opportunities rather than credit-bearing requirements, with engineering study away dependent on suitable courses.
programmes.ib: No programme-specific IB grade threshold is published on the reviewed page; mathematics and science preparation are important for the curriculum.

programmes.name: Social Research and Public Policy
programmes.about: Social theory and research methods used to investigate inequality, development and public policy.
programmes.overview: You connect economics, politics, sociology, development and anthropology with quantitative and qualitative research. Foundational courses examine social thought and global development before more focused study. The capstone is an original research project developed with a faculty mentor; it may use new data, simulations or existing datasets. The programme develops the ability to judge evidence, frame policy questions and evaluate interventions, including issues relevant to the Gulf.

notes: NYUAD awards four-year NYU BA/BS degrees. The degree combines at least 128 credits with a first-year writing seminar, the Core, a major, two January Terms and a capstone. Majors are declared by the end of year two, although some sequences begin in year one.

IB exams do not earn degree credit at NYUAD. Prior IB study can sometimes support placement into a more advanced course, at the academic dean’s and subject faculty’s discretion, possibly after a placement test. Placement does not reduce the total courses required; keep your official IB results for the review.

These three programmes are sourced examples within the broader catalogue, not the whole English-taught portfolio. The major pages encourage mathematical preparation; the reviewed admissions pages do not publish a numerical IB minimum or mandatory IB subject/grade combination. Recommended preparation is not an entry threshold.

IB documents: the NYU qualifications tool requests four years of school transcripts, including current grades, and predictions for six IB subjects. After admission, send final IB results electronically from the IBO; the final Diploma meets proof of graduation without ECE verification. Applicants who already graduated submit final results when applying. A 2027 final-document deadline is not recorded: the admitted-student hub still says 15 July 2026, so that date has not been rolled forward.

DP Course Results alone are not established as a school-leaving qualification by the reviewed IB Diploma guidance. They are not automatically rejected either: ask NYUAD which separate final secondary-school qualification it would require for your case.
Standardized testing remains optional through the 2027–28 application cycle. This does not remove school records, required English proof or final graduation documents.

English proof: non-native speakers generally need a recent test unless all their subjects, except world languages, were taught solely in English for the preceding three years. NYUAD also warns that most non-native speakers should expect testing even after English-medium study and may request proof from anyone. A two-year IB is not an automatic exemption. The linked central test list could not be read during this check, so exact accepted tests and score guidance remain a question for admissions.

The application has a USD 85 fee, with a waiver request available. Complete the Common Application, school report, recommendation, STARS academic record and NYUAD Applicant Profile. The portal can take 7–10 business days; NYUAD recommends submitting the Common Application about a month before the chosen deadline.

Selection considers academics, sustained extracurricular work, recommendations and community contribution. Invited finalists must attend Candidate Weekend and confirm within 48 hours. It includes an interview and additional assessments; NYUAD pays participation travel, visa, accommodation and meals where needed. An invitation does not guarantee admission.

For the explicitly published 2026–27 application cycle, Candidate Weekends are 11–13 December 2026, 5–7 February 2027 and 19–21 March 2027. The waitlist weekend on 24–25 April 2027 is virtual. Attend the assigned round; changes are not guaranteed.

The application and CSS tables give month/day without a year. Their 2026/2027 years are mapped to the published application cycle and remain provisional in this record. The listed notification pattern is 15 December, 15 February and 1 April. Confirm the dates and 23:59 EST cut-off in the applicant portal.

Early Decision is binding if admitted with an affordable aid package; withdraw other applications and accept within 2–3 weeks. NYUAD permits release for insufficient aid and for an offer to a non-primary NYU choice. A denied Early Decision applicant cannot apply again in another NYU round that cycle.
Applicants must be at least 17 by 1 August of the enrollment year. NYUAD has an on-campus residential requirement; adult applicants should consider whether that setting fits them.

2026–27 annual tuition is USD 68,574 and the estimated autumn/spring cost of attendance is USD 90,434 before aid. That budget includes USD 6,000 housing, USD 5,800 food, USD 2,416 insurance and USD 1,730 books; travel and personal costs are estimates. January Term and summer costs are separate. No 2027–28 price is published on the reviewed page; do not treat these figures as a 2027 quote.

For non-Emirati citizens, including EU/EEA applicants, NYUAD grants depend on assessed financial need; there is no EU tuition discount stated here. The admission award is normally renewed at the same level subject to renewal requirements, with no routine later reassessment. The reviewed pages do not confirm need-blind admission, so this record makes no such promise.

Aid applicants use CSS code 2785 and, where required, separate custodial and noncustodial parent Profiles or an approved waiver. The CSS deadlines are 10 November, 10 January and 1 February for the corresponding rounds. Supply additional financial documents through IDOC only when requested. The autumn 2027 verification page asks for 2025 income evidence, with English translations where required.

Housing is in gender-separated residential floors with resident assistants. First-year students cannot request particular roommates; approved accessibility needs are considered. The current published charge is USD 3,000 per autumn/spring semester, included in the older annual budget above. A single room is not promised.

Academic planning, peer tutoring, writing and English support are available. The Moses Center coordinates accessibility adjustments, the Health and Wellness Center offers care and counselling, and the Career Development Center helps with internships, employment and further study. Follow the source links for the appropriate office.
